settings.title: Settings
settings.autoLockHint: The vault also locks when Windows locks, when the screen turns off and when the computer sleeps.
settings.kitUnknown: No Emergency Kit has been created on this computer yet.
settings.kitNewExplain: A new recovery key replaces the old one. Destroy your old Emergency Kit afterwards.
settings.rotateIntro: Use this if your master password or recovery key may have been exposed. It replaces the key that encrypts your vault.
rotateExplain: Your vault is re-encrypted with a new key and you get a new recovery key (new Emergency Kit).
Your master password stays the same. Change it as well if it may have been exposed.
The old recovery key stops working for the vault from now on.
Older copies of the vault (the backups folder) still open with the old password and recovery key. Delete them if they may be exposed.
settings.closeToTray: Close button hides xPass to the tray
settings.lockOnMinimize: Lock when xPass is minimized or hidden to the tray
settings.rotateExplainHello: Windows Hello is turned off. You can set it up again right after.
settings.rotateExplainSync: Sync is on: the new vault is uploaded to GitHub first, so this needs a working connection. Your other PCs then ask for the master password once.

password.tooWeak: Choose a stronger password to continue.

strength.hint: Use 4 or more random words, or 12+ mixed characters.

setup.title: Create your vault
setup.intro: Choose a master password. It encrypts your vault and is never stored or sent anywhere. If you forget it, only your Emergency Kit can open the vault.

kit.title: Your Emergency Kit
kit.intro: This recovery key opens your vault if you forget the master password. It is shown only now. Print it or save it as a PDF, and keep it offline somewhere safe.
kit.warning: Anyone with this key and your vault file can read your passwords.
kit.confirmIntro: Type groups {{a}} and {{b}} of your recovery key.
kit.confirmMismatch: These groups do not match. Check your Emergency Kit.
kit.printHowTo: If you forget your master password
printSteps: Open xPass and choose “Use recovery key” on the unlock screen.
Type the recovery key above. Dashes, spaces and letter case do not matter.
kit.printKeep: Keep this sheet offline. Do not store it on the same computer or in the same cloud account as your vault.

unlock.title: Unlock xPass
unlock.useRecovery: Forgot your password? Use recovery key

lockReason.idle: Locked after a period of inactivity.
lockReason.displayOff: Locked because the screen turned off (sleep or display timeout).
lockReason.suspend: Locked because the computer went to sleep.
lockReason.minimized: Locked because xPass was minimized or hidden.

recovery.title: Unlock with recovery key
recovery.intro: Enter the recovery key from your Emergency Kit.

newPassword.title: Set a new master password
newPassword.intro: You unlocked the vault with the recovery key. Choose a new master password to continue.
newPassword.kitIntro: Your old recovery key still works. Create a new kit if the old one was lost or someone else may have seen it.

copy.secret: Copied. Clears from the clipboard in {{seconds}} s.

generator.noSet: Choose at least one character set.

entries.selectHint: Select an entry to see its details.
entries.emptyHint: Your vault is empty. Create your first entry.

hello.title: Windows Hello
hello.intro: Unlock xPass with your face, fingerprint or PIN. Your master password keeps working and is still needed for sensitive changes.
hello.stateOn: Windows Hello is on for this vault.
hello.unavailable: Windows Hello is not set up on this PC. Set up a PIN, face or fingerprint in Windows Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options, then come back here.
hello.unavailableEnrolled: Windows Hello is not available on this PC right now. Unlock with your master password; you can turn Windows Hello off here.
hello.turnOnExplain: Enter your master password. Windows Hello then asks you to confirm it is you.
hello.turnOffMessage: You will unlock xPass with your master password only. You can turn Windows Hello on again at any time.
hello.reenrollMessage: The vault key was changed or Windows Hello was reset on this PC, so Windows Hello no longer unlocks this vault.
hello.keyChangePending: The vault key was changed on another device. Enter the master password in the sync notice first, then turn Windows Hello on.

sync.title: Sync
sync.intro: Keep this vault in sync across your PCs through a file in a private GitHub repository. Only the encrypted vault is uploaded; GitHub never sees your passwords or your master password.
sync.needsToken: Sync is off until a GitHub token is saved. Choose Change and enter a token.
sync.testFirst: Test the connection before saving. The token is stored in Windows Credential Manager and never shown again.
sync.disconnectMessage: The token is deleted from this PC and xPass stops syncing. Your vault on this PC and the copy on GitHub are not changed.

report.missing: Connected. There is no vault at this path yet; the first sync will create it on branch {{branch}}.
report.sameVault: Connected. This vault is already stored at this path.
report.found: Connected. An xPass vault was found at this path.
report.otherVault: A different xPass vault is stored at this path. Choose another path, or another repository.
report.notAVault: This path holds a file that is not an xPass vault. Choose another path.
report.branchMissing: The branch {{branch}} does not exist in this repository.
report.public: This repository is public. The vault is encrypted, but anyone can download it and its full history. A private repository is strongly recommended.
report.publicAck: I understand and want to use this public repository.
report.joinMissing: Connected, but there is no vault at this path. Check the branch and path used on your other PC.

guide.title: How to create a GitHub token
steps: Create a private repository on GitHub for the vault (an empty one is fine).
Open GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens, and choose Generate new token.
Repository access: Only select repositories, and pick the vault repository.
Permissions: Contents: Read and write (Metadata: Read-only is added automatically).
Choose an expiration date, generate the token and paste it here. You can replace it here when it expires.
guide.note: Use a token that can only reach this one repository. Do not reuse a token with wider access.

status.pending: Changes on this PC are not synced yet.
status.offline: Offline. Changes are kept on this PC and synced later.
status.noToken: Sync is off until a GitHub token is saved on this PC.
status.tokenInvalid: Sync stopped: the GitHub token needs to be replaced.
status.needsPassword: Sync stopped: the vault key was changed on another device. Your master password is needed.
status.differentVault: Sync stopped: GitHub holds a different vault at this path.
status.error: Sync failed; it will be retried.

join.title: Use your vault from GitHub
join.intro: Already using xPass on another PC with GitHub sync? Enter the same repository and a GitHub token, then your master password. The vault is downloaded and opened on this PC.
join.doneTitle: Your vault is on this PC
join.done: The vault was downloaded and sync is on.
join.kitReminder: Your existing Emergency Kit still opens this vault; no new kit is needed. Changes on this PC and your other PCs are synced through GitHub.
join.helloOffer: Windows Hello can unlock the vault on this PC with your face, fingerprint or PIN.

syncProblem.passwordChangedTitle: Master password changed on another device
syncProblem.passwordChanged: Use the new master password the next time you unlock xPass on this PC. Windows Hello keeps working.
syncProblem.tokenTitle: GitHub token expired or lacks access
syncProblem.token: Sync is paused. Your changes stay on this PC. Enter a new token in Sync settings.
syncProblem.tokenInSettings: Sync is paused. Your changes stay on this PC. Choose Change and enter a new token.
syncProblem.keyTitle: Vault key changed on another device
syncProblem.key: The vault key was replaced on another PC, so sync is paused. Enter the master password to continue. Changes made on this PC are kept.
syncProblem.keyExplain: Enter the master password as it is now on the other PC. Your changes on this PC are merged and synced.
syncProblem.other: The file at this path belongs to another vault, so sync stopped. Use another path in Sync settings, or replace this PC’s vault with the one on GitHub.
syncProblem.otherInSettings: The file at this path belongs to another vault, so sync stopped. Choose Change to use another path, or replace this PC’s vault with the one on GitHub.
syncProblem.replacePassword: Master password of the vault on GitHub
replaceExplain: This PC’s vault is replaced by the vault on GitHub. Entries that exist only on this PC are no longer shown.
The current vault file is kept in the backups folder.
From now on, unlock with the master password of the vault on GitHub.
syncProblem.replaced: This PC now uses the vault from GitHub.

restore.title: Restore a previous version
restore.intro: xPass keeps the last 10 versions of your vault on this PC, one per save. Restoring one puts your entries back as they were then.

kind.olderKey: Saved before the vault key was changed
kind.otherVault: Another vault; cannot be restored here

restore.explain: Your entries are put back as they were on {{date}}: entries added later are deleted, changed entries get their old content back (the current values stay in their history).
restore.keepCurrent: The current version is kept, so you can undo this here.
restore.syncs: The restore is saved as a new change and syncs to your other devices.
restore.olderKeyExplain: This version was saved before the vault key was changed. Enter the master password it was saved with. Your current password and key stay as they are.

import.title: Import from CSV
import.intro: Bring in passwords exported from Bitwarden, Chrome or Edge, KeePassXC, xPass, or any CSV file. You see a preview before anything is saved.
import.mappingIntro: Choose which column holds each field. The preview updates when you change a column.
import.countSkipped_one: {{count}} empty or unsupported row left out
import.countSkipped_other: {{count}} empty or unsupported rows left out
import.possibleQuestion_one: {{count}} entry has the same site and username as an existing one, but a different password:
import.possibleQuestion_other: {{count}} entries have the same site and username as existing ones, but a different password:

duplicates.update: Update the existing entries (the old password is kept in their history)

warnings.titleFromUrl: No title in the file; the website is used.
warnings.titleFromUsername: No title or website in the file; the username is used.
warnings.invalidDate: The creation date could not be read; today is used.
warnings.invalidFields: The custom fields could not be read and were left out.

import.undoHint: To undo this import, use Settings → Restore a previous version and pick the version saved just before it.
import.deleteHint: The CSV file is not encrypted: anyone who can read it sees your passwords. Delete it when you no longer need it.
import.deleteMessage: xPass deletes the file it imported. This is a normal delete: on SSDs the data cannot be wiped reliably. If the file was in the Recycle Bin or synced to a cloud folder, empty those too.

export.title: Export
export.intro: Save a copy of your entries to use in another password manager. Every export asks for your master password or Windows Hello.
export.csvWarning: A CSV file is not encrypted. Anyone who can read the file sees all your passwords.
csvRules: Do not open it in Excel or another spreadsheet app: they can change values and keep copies.
Do not save it in a folder that syncs to the cloud.
Delete it as soon as you have imported it elsewhere.
export.understand: I understand that this file is not protected
export.kdbxExplain: The KeePass file is encrypted with an export password. Choose a new one; do not reuse your master password. You need it to open the file in KeePass or KeePassXC.
export.authExplain: Enter your master password to export the vault. Next, choose where to save the file.
export.csvAfter: This file is not encrypted. Move it where you need it and delete it after use. Empty the Recycle Bin afterwards.
export.kdbxAfter: Keep the export password somewhere safe: without it the file cannot be opened.

history.useMessage: It becomes the current password. The current password is kept in the history.

update.confirmMessage: xPass downloads the update and checks its signature. It then locks the vault, sends unsynced changes to GitHub and closes; the installer replaces the app and starts it again. You unlock with your password or Windows Hello as usual.
update.onStartup: Check for updates when xPass starts (at most once a day)
update.hint: The check only reads the latest version and its signed release data from GitHub. Nothing is downloaded or installed until you choose Install and restart.
